## Proof

We determine the cardinality of the set $\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb{N}, \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{N}))$ of injective functions $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{N})$.

**Upper bound.** Every injective function is in particular a function, so
$$\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb{N},\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{N}))\;\subseteq\;\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{N})^{\mathbb{N}}.$$
Hence
$$\left|\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb{N},\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{N}))\right|\;\le\;\left|\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{N})^{\mathbb{N}}\right|=\left(2^{\aleph_{0}}\right)^{\aleph_{0}}=2^{\aleph_{0}\cdot\aleph_{0}}=2^{\aleph_{0}}.$$

**Lower bound.** We exhibit an injection $\{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb{N},\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{N}))$, which gives cardinality $\ge 2^{\aleph_{0}}$.

For each binary sequence $x=(x_{0},x_{1},x_{2},\dots)\in\{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}}$, define $f_{x}:\mathbb{N}\to\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{N})$ by
$$f_{x}(0)=\{\,2n : x_{n}=1\,\}\quad(\text{a subset of the even numbers}),$$
$$f_{x}(k)=\{2k-1\}\quad\text{for }k\ge 1\quad(\text{the singleton of the odd number }2k-1).$$

*Injectivity of each $f_{x}$:* For $k,\ell\ge 1$ with $k\ne\ell$, the singletons $\{2k-1\}$ and $\{2\ell-1\}$ are distinct. Also $f_{x}(0)$ is a subset of the even numbers, so it is never equal to any singleton $\{2k-1\}$ of an odd number (a subset of evens cannot contain an odd element, while $\{2k-1\}$ does). Thus all values $f_{x}(0),f_{x}(1),f_{x}(2),\dots$ are pairwise distinct, i.e. $f_{x}\in\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb{N},\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{N}))$.

*Injectivity of the map $x\mapsto f_{x}$:* If $x\ne y$, then $f_{x}(0)=\{2n:x_{n}=1\}\ne\{2n:y_{n}=1\}=f_{y}(0)$, so $f_{x}\ne f_{y}$.

Therefore
$$\left|\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb{N},\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{N}))\right|\;\ge\;\left|\{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}}\right|=2^{\aleph_{0}}.$$

**Conclusion.** Combining the upper and lower bounds,
$$\left|\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb{N},\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{N}))\right|=2^{\aleph_{0}},$$
the cardinality of the continuum.

### PROOF COMPLETE
